channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visits Kyrgyzstan for SCO summit and related meetings
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev traveled to Bishkek on August 31 for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting and an 'SCO plus' format encounter. Discussions will focus on SCO development and regional cooperation, including bilateral meetings and the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Seeks Easing of US Visa Bond Requirements
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan met with U.S. Special Envoy Sergio Gor to discuss simplifying visa requirements for Kyrgyz citizens traveling to the United States. They specifically addressed reviewing the visa bond requirement and other restrictions. Gor expressed readiness to strengthen Kyrgyzstan-USA relations and discussed political dialogue, trade, and investment cooperation.

item.title: SCO Summit and State Visits to Bishkek: Developments Today
item.description: Bishkek is hosting events related to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit and official visits by heads of state on August 31 and September 1, expecting 21 presidents and prime ministers. Unprecedented security measures are in place. The SCO marks its 25th anniversary, with the summit on September 1. Meetings between Armenian and Azerbaijani leaders, and the arrival of the Pakistani Prime Minister are noted.

item.title: Armenian PM Pashinyan Reports Meeting with Azerbaijani President Aliyev in Bishkek
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced on social media that he met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Bishkek. Pashinyan shared footage of the negotiations. Further details about the meeting and the topics discussed were not immediately available. Both leaders are in Kyrgyzstan to attend the SCO Plus high-level meeting and the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.

item.title: Afghanistan does not pose a threat to neighboring countries, says Taliban representative
item.description: A representative of Afghanistan's interim government, Zabihullah Mujahid, responded to statements about supplying weapons to the Tajikistan-Afghanistan border. Mujahid stated that Afghanistan does not pose a threat to its neighbors. This statement comes after reports of an agreement to strengthen the border.

item.title: Kyrgyz President invites UN to co-organize Global Mountain Summit in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres to discuss cooperation and the global mountain and climate agenda. Japarov proposed the UN co-organize the 2nd Global Mountain Summit in Bishkek from October 21-23, 2027, to broaden international participation.

item.title: Pakistan Culture Days to be held in Tajikistan in 2027
item.description: Pakistan Culture Days will take place in Tajikistan in 2027 as part of cultural cooperation. The event aims to introduce Tajikistan's residents to Pakistani culture, art, and literature. Meetings with cultural representatives and exhibitions are planned.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev travels to Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has departed for Bishkek on a working visit. He will attend the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and a "SCO Plus" format meeting on August 31.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Calls US Economic War Against Tehran a "Failed Policy"
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described US President Donald Trump's threat to initiate an economic war against Tehran as a continuation of Washington's "failed policies." This statement criticizes the US approach to economic pressure on Iran.

item.title: Yerlan Karin Appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree appointing Yerlan Karin as the country's Vice President. The appointment follows parliamentary approval, with 141 out of 145 deputies supporting Karin's nomination. This new role was established under the new constitution.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at the airport by Kyrgyzstan's acting Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev and other officials. The presidential press service reported on the arrival.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New Funding Rules for Private Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education has proposed new rules for funding private schools that operate under the state order. The ministry suggests establishing a fixed funding amount, independent of the annual increase in the monthly calculated indicator (MRP), to ensure educational accessibility and stability.

item.title: Infrastructure Development Fund Established as Treasury Account in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Infrastructure Development Fund will operate as a special account within the state treasury, rather than a separate organization. This fund will finance major national infrastructure projects, with payments disbursed in stages based on work completion, as reported by Orda.kz.

item.title: China proposes 'Water Silk Road' via Irtysh River for Arctic access
item.description: China, Kazakhstan, and Russia are discussing a project to transform the Irtysh River into a cargo corridor with Arctic access, dubbed the 'Water Silk Road'. This route, originating in China and flowing through Kazakhstan and Russia to the Arctic Ocean, could offer China an alternative to vulnerable maritime routes. Infrastructure development, including dams and dredging, would be necessary.

item.title: First Direct Flight from Dushanbe to Minsk Celebrated with Water Arch Ceremony
item.description: A Somon Air flight from Dushanbe to Minsk was welcomed with a traditional water arch ceremony at Minsk National Airport. This new direct route marks a significant step in strengthening relations, promoting tourism, and fostering trade between Tajikistan and Belarus.

item.title: Two Dead After Pleasure Boat Crashes into Rock in Aktau
item.description: A pleasure boat carrying seven people collided with a rock in the Caspian Sea near Aktau, resulting in two fatalities. Rescuers recovered the bodies of two individuals approximately 500 meters offshore, while five passengers were brought to shore and received medical attention.

item.title: New rules for handling archaeological finds in Kazakhstan require preservation for three years
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced new regulations for archaeologists on storing and transferring excavated artifacts. The rules prohibit cleaning items with household chemicals, drying them by fire, or gluing them with makeshift materials. Metal objects must be extracted with soil, and ceramic fragments with soot should not be washed.

item.title: Repressions in Central Asia: Purge victims, imprisoned women, and fate of children
item.description: According to NKVD data, plans for repression in Central Asia targeted 224,400 individuals. Uzbekistan SSR was allocated quotas for 4,750 people: 750 for execution and 4,000 for imprisonment. The article details the reasons for women's imprisonment and the fate of children.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon departs for SCO summit in Bishkek
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon departed for Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the summit of heads of state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). He was seen off at Dushanbe International Airport by high-ranking officials. He is accompanied by several ministers.

item.title: Kazakhstan mining firms can adjust procurement costs due to weak tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Industry and Construction has allowed mining companies to recalculate procurement costs based on the tenge's exchange rate. This applies to contracts signed before or during payment. Suppliers must demonstrate how the exchange rate affects costs.

item.title: Russian MoD announces preparation for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Defense stated on August 30 that the armed forces are preparing massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities. The ministry claims these actions are a response to ongoing Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and its fuel-energy complex.

item.title: Uzbekistan's UN Resident Coordinator reflects on two years of changes and climate challenges
item.description: Akiko Fujii, the UN Development Programme Resident Representative in Uzbekistan, reflects on her two years in the country. She notes the impact of climate change, with over 25% of land degraded and nearly 45% at risk of desertification. Recent water reforms are seen as a positive step.

item.title: US strikes Iranian missile launchers; Tehran targets US bases in Jordan
item.description: On August 30, US forces attacked Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, Iran reportedly launched missile strikes against US military bases 'King Hussein' and 'Al-Azraq' in Jordan.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Immediate Payment for Public Bus Fares from September 1
item.description: Starting September 1, passengers in Uzbekistan must pay bus fares immediately upon boarding. This applies to buses operating under gross contracts. Previously, electronic ticket payments could be made until the end of the trip. The state institution for monitoring passenger transport in Tashkent explained the new regulation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Appoints New Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan. The decree was signed by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Aripov replaces Erlan Abdildaev, who was previously released from this post and appointed Ambassador to Hungary.

item.title: UN Secretary-General António Guterres Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has arrived in Kyrgyzstan to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Minister of Economy and Commerce, Bakyt Sydykov. Guterres will attend the Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek.

item.title: 12 Uzbek children without parental care returned from Russia
item.description: Twelve underage Uzbek citizens, deprived of parental care or in difficult social situations, have been returned to Uzbekistan from various regions of Russia. The repatriation was a collaborative effort involving the Uzbek embassy, ministries of internal affairs and health, and the National Agency for Social Protection. This year, 38 children have been repatriated from Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day. Mirziyoyev noted Kyrgyzstan's economic and social growth under Japarov's leadership and highlighted the elevated bilateral relations to a "union level." He also emphasized the importance of regional cooperation and upcoming events.

item.title: Hong Kong banks may finance Tashkent-Samarkand toll road project
item.description: Hong Kong banks are considering financing the construction of the Tashkent-Samarkand toll road. The potential involvement of Hong Kong financial institutions was discussed by Uzbekistan's Transport Minister Ilkhom Makhkamov and the head of Hong Kong's "Belt and Road" Office, Nicholas Ho Lik-chi. Prospects for air travel and economic cooperation were also discussed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker congratulates nation on Independence Day
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, congratulated Kyrgyzstan's citizens on the 35th anniversary of Independence. He emphasized that strengthening independence is a duty and highlighted the country's progress in economic, state, and international spheres under President Sadyr Japarov. The Speaker wished for peace, unity, and prosperity.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Secretary Links Xi Jinping's Visit to Ancient Monk's Journey
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Arslan Koichiev drew a historical parallel between Xi Jinping's visit and the 7th-century monk Xuanzang's journey. Koichiev noted Xi's visit to the same location Xuanzang stayed and referenced Xi's article on Kyrgyzstan-China relations, highlighting historical figures who fostered cultural exchange.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Asked US to Lead Anti-Houthi War, Washington Refused
item.description: Saudi Arabia requested the United States to lead a war against the Houthis, but Washington declined. This issue was raised during a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Admiral Brad Cooper, head of the US Central Command, on August 14.

item.title: US President Trump Congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: US President Donald Trump sent congratulations to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on their Independence Day. He highlighted the strong relationship built on mutual respect, economic ties, and shared commitment to regional security. The US reaffirms its support for Kyrgyzstan's sovereignty and independence.

item.title: Leaders of Several Countries Congratulate Kyrgyzstan on 35th Independence Anniversary
item.description: Heads of state from Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Belgium, Iran, Pakistan, Egypt, Belarus, Azerbaijan, and Turkey, along with Armenia's Prime Minister, congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its 35th Independence Day. They wished the nation peace and prosperity and President Japarov good health and success. Several leaders expressed eagerness to deepen bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh President: Kyrgyzstan Has Successfully Developed Since Independence
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day, noting its growing authority, evidenced by its UN Security Council election. He highlighted reforms for economic growth and praised the fraternal relations between Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organization Celebrates 25 Years, Drives Regional Economic Cooperation
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) marks its 25th anniversary, having grown into a major international body with 27 member states and a GDP nearing $30 trillion. The SCO actively promotes trade, energy, transport, and digital economy projects, enhancing regional stability and global governance.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Bishkek for State Visit and SCO Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife were welcomed in Bishkek by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Xi Jinping conveyed greetings to the Kyrgyz people, highlighting the long-standing friendship and stable development of bilateral relations, now at a high level of comprehensive partnership.

item.title: Britain warns companies supplying arms to Ukraine about Russian attack risks
item.description: British government officials have informed defense company leaders about increased threats from the Kremlin against them and their staff. This warning comes as companies supply arms to Ukraine, highlighting potential Russian attack risks.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island; Iran retaliates against US bases in Jordan
item.description: The US conducted strikes on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting forces preparing to mine the strait. Iran's IRGC claimed to have retaliated by striking two US military bases in Jordan, targeting infrastructure and fighter jets.

item.title: New Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway shows significant damage after construction
item.description: Activists report significant damage to the new Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway, including asphalt degradation and foundation issues, less than two years after its completion. The road, built with Chinese loans, cost over 180 billion tenge and has a two-year warranty.
